children: REIT investors are finding opportunities in property sectors tied to demographic and housing trends, although some areas remain more challenging as financing costs stay elevated.
David Auerbach of Hoya Capital, in an interview with Seeking Alpha's
, said the firm was particularly focused on healthcare REITs, including senior housing and medical office, while remaining selective on office, apartments, and single-family rentals.

Auerbach said the senior housing market could benefit from rising demand as the first baby boomers turn 80, while supply remains insufficient to meet that demand. He also pointed to manufactured housing, industrial, storage, and single-family rental as sectors where net operating income has grown since 2019, with manufactured housing recording 49% growth over that period.
Single-family rental fundamentals were also improving as competing supply slowed, Auerbach said. He cited Invitation Homes
as an example, while noting that housing regulation remained a risk for the sector.

Auerbach was particularly cautious on commercial mortgage REITs, citing dividend coverage and the resolution of underlying credit as the two main concerns. He said loan resolutions had remained below previous reserve values in parts of the sector, with stress visible in office, multifamily bridge, and life-science markets.
However, he said residential mortgage REIT dividend coverage had generally improved over the last quarter and cautioned against treating the entire mortgage REIT universe as one trade.

title: Senior housing, office, and rentals draw selective REIT interest
